sets.offline_line: {sets} is offline; the values are from the last reading.
sets.pack_power_note: Power on the battery side · − = delivering
sets.cell_note: Cell difference = highest minus lowest cell voltage in the battery (the set reports per 10 mV). In the middle of the charge it says little: the voltage of LiFePO4 is flat there. It is judged when the battery is (nearly) full with a small current (at most 0.1 C): up to 30 mV Good, up to 100 mV Balancing (normal near full; the set works it away), above that Imbalance.
sets.activity_title: What the set did · last 24 hours
sets.no_activity: No quarters in the cost log yet.
sets.line_now: {pack} is out of balance now ({mv} mV). Let the set charge fully a few times.
sets.line_recent: {pack} was out of balance on {day} ({mv} mV); that usually evens out after a full charge.
sets.line_persistent: {pack} stays out of balance ({days} of the last 7 days). Let the set charge fully a few times; if it stays, contact Zendure.
sets.line_not_full: the batteries were not (nearly) full this week, so the cell difference was not judged.
sets.not_judged_title: The cell difference is judged when the battery is (nearly) full and the current is small.
sets.days_title: What the battery did per day · last 7 days
sets.days_note: kWh at the battery side of the inverter (AC) · today so far
sets.days_explain: Cycles = delivered ÷ usable capacity ({usable} kWh between the limits). Efficiency = delivered ÷ charged over the week, corrected for the change in SoC. From the cost log, per closed quarter.

settings.title: Settings

groups.zero_meter: Zero on the meter without planner

settings.readonly: Only an administrator can change settings.
settings.reload_note: Changes in this group are saved together; ZEPHYR then restarts briefly.
settings.supplier_note: With a supplier the amounts from the tariff table apply ({source}). The greyed-out fields show those amounts; they can only be changed with own tariffs.

min_soc.label: Minimum state of charge
min_soc.help: Below this the battery stops delivering.
min_soc.more: Default 10 %; common 5–15 %. Lower = more usable energy, but the battery is more often nearly empty. ZEPHYR also sets this in the set, so it stops when ZEPHYR is not running. Example: 11 kWh and 10 % → 1.1 kWh always stays.

max_soc.label: Maximum state of charge
max_soc.help: Above this the battery stops charging.
max_soc.more: Default 95 %; 90–95 % saves a little wear, 100 % gives about 5 % more usable energy. Now and then the set needs 100 % to reset its SOC reading and balance the cells; see Calibration after days.

p1_source.label: P1 measurement
p1_source.help: One sensor with net power, or import and export separately.
p1_source.more: Choose One sensor if your meter gives one power that goes negative when exporting (usually a P1 dongle such as HomeWizard). Choose Import and export with two separate sensors (DSMR integration). The more often the meter reports, the better: DSMR 5 reports every second, DSMR 4 every 10 s. If the meter is silent for more than 10 s, ZEPHYR stops safely.

p1_entity.label: P1 sensor (net)
p1_entity.more: A power sensor in W or kW, positive when importing. For example Active power of a HomeWizard P1 meter. Not the kWh counter.

p1_import_entity.label: P1 import
p1_import_entity.more: For example Power consumption of the DSMR integration (in kW or W). ZEPHYR uses import − export.

p1_export_entity.label: P1 export
p1_export_entity.more: For example Power production of the DSMR integration. Must belong to the same meter as the import sensor.

price_entity.label: Price sensor
price_entity.help: Nord Pool: the HACS integration, or the current price of Home Assistant's own Nord Pool integration.
price_entity.more: For example the Nord Pool integration (HACS) or HA's own Nord Pool integration, area NL, prices per quarter without taxes (ZEPHYR adds markup, tax and VAT itself). Tomorrow's prices arrive around 13:00. Without a price sensor ZEPHYR makes no plan and only keeps the meter at zero.

solar_forecast_entity.label: Solar forecast
solar_forecast_entity.help: Solcast (tomorrow) with half-hour detail. Empty: the solar forecast of HA's Energy dashboard.
solar_forecast_entity.more: Recommended: Solcast (free for home use), most precise per half hour. Leaving it empty works with any source in HA's Energy dashboard (Forecast.Solar, Open-Meteo …), per hour. Without a forecast the planner uses yesterday's yield.

solar_energy_entity.label: Solar counter
solar_energy_entity.more: Your inverter's increasing kWh counter, e.g. Lifetime energy of SolarEdge. The same as Solar panels in the Energy dashboard. Used for house consumption, the cost log and tuning the solar forecast.

excluded_energy_entity.label: Air conditioner: energy counter
excluded_energy_entity.help: kWh counter of a load the battery may not feed.
excluded_energy_entity.more: A kWh counter of the air conditioner only, e.g. from a smart plug or sub-meter, or the energy sensor of the air conditioner integration. ZEPHYR does not deliver for it while it runs in a blocked mode; the rest of the house still comes from the battery.

excluded_climate_entity.label: Air conditioner: climate entity
excluded_climate_entity.help: Says at once whether it runs and in which mode.
excluded_climate_entity.more: The air conditioner's climate entity. With it ZEPHYR sees right away whether it is on and whether it heats or cools. Without: it never comes from the battery and ZEPHYR only notices a stop from the counter.

excluded_hvac_modes.label: Air conditioner: not from the battery when
excluded_hvac_modes.help: Modes in which the battery does not feed it.
excluded_hvac_modes.more: Default heating: in winter the air conditioner uses a lot, and grid power is then often cheaper than battery power. Also choose cooling if it must never come from the battery.

cost_import_counters.label: Import counters
cost_import_counters.help: The kWh counters of your smart meter (tariff 1 and 2).
cost_import_counters.more: Choose both kWh counters of your smart meter: Energy consumption (tarif 1) and (tarif 2). More precise than adding up power; for the cost log and savings.

cost_export_counters.label: Export counters
cost_export_counters.help: The kWh counters for export (tariff 1 and 2).
cost_export_counters.more: Choose both export counters: Energy production (tarif 1) and (tarif 2). For the cost log.

tariff_supplier.label: Energy supplier
tariff_supplier.help: Amounts from ZEPHYR's tariff table, or own tariffs.
tariff_supplier.more: If your supplier is in the list, choose it: tax, markups and solar bonus then come from the table and follow new tariffs. If not, choose Own tariffs and enter the amounts from your contract.

tariff_energy_tax.label: Energy tax
tariff_energy_tax.more: Statutory amount per kWh, without VAT; now {in_use}. Changes every year on 1 January; with a supplier from the table that happens automatically.

tariff_markup_import.label: Import margin
tariff_markup_import.help: What the supplier adds to the market price, excluding VAT.
tariff_markup_import.more: What the supplier charges per kWh on top of the market price, without VAT. Common € 0.01–0.03; Zonneplan € 0.01653. On your contract or tariff sheet, sometimes as purchase fee.

tariff_markup_export.label: Export margin
tariff_markup_export.help: Added to the market price (negative = a fee), excluding VAT.
tariff_markup_export.more: What you get per exported kWh on top of the market price, without VAT. If your supplier deducts something (export fee), enter it negative, e.g. −0.02. Zonneplan + € 0.01653.

tariff_vat.label: VAT
tariff_vat.help: On market price, margin and energy tax.
tariff_vat.more: Statutory rate, 21 % in the Netherlands. Applies to market price, markup and energy tax.

tariff_solar_bonus.label: Solar bonus
tariff_solar_bonus.help: Extra on the export price during the day.
tariff_solar_bonus.more: Extra percentage on the export price while the sun is up, e.g. 10 % at Zonneplan. No solar bonus: 0.

tariff_fixed_month.label: Fixed costs per month
tariff_fixed_month.help: Supply and network costs minus tax credit.
tariff_fixed_month.more: Fixed supply charge + grid operator charge − energy tax reduction, per month including VAT. On your annual bill or tariff sheet. Only for the cost log; does not change the plan.

plan_wear_cost.label: Wear cost
plan_wear_cost.more: Default € 0.03 per kWh: roughly the purchase price divided by what the battery delivers in its life (e.g. € 3,000 / 6,000 cycles / 10 kWh ≈ € 0.05). Higher = the battery only works at larger price differences.

plan_grid_charge_cost.label: Grid charging threshold
plan_grid_charge_cost.help: Minimum gain per kWh to charge from the grid.
plan_grid_charge_cost.more: Default € 0.01. Charging from the grid only happens when it earns at least this much per kWh, after losses and wear. Higher = less often charging from the grid for a small gain.

plan_allow_export.label: Export from the battery
plan_allow_export.help: May the battery deliver to the grid when that pays?
plan_allow_export.more: Default off. On only makes sense if the export price is sometimes higher than what recharging costs later, including about 15 % loss and wear. With net metering (until 2027) it rarely pays.

plan_load_margin.label: Consumption margin
plan_load_margin.help: Plan with more consumption than learned.
plan_load_margin.more: Default 0 %; 5–15 % if the battery runs empty too early on busy evenings. The planner then counts on that much more consumption than learned.

plan_buffer.label: Buffer
plan_buffer.help: Part of the battery the planner keeps free.
plan_buffer.more: Default 0 %; e.g. 10 % if you want a reserve for unexpected consumption. The planner does not plan this part; the controller may use it when consumption turns out higher. The planner then refills it when that is cheap.

expensive_hours.label: Expensive hours
expensive_hours.help: Without planner: only deliver in the N most expensive hours.
expensive_hours.more: Default 4: the battery only delivers in the 4 most expensive hours of the day and holds its charge otherwise. Only in the mode Zero on the meter with a price sensor; Dynamic Forecasting chooses itself.

reserve_soc.label: Reserve
reserve_soc.help: Without planner: charge to this level before the expensive hours.
reserve_soc.more: Default 20 %: before the expensive hours ZEPHYR charges up to this percentage. Only without the planner; with Dynamic Forecasting it counts as buffer.

min_price.label: Minimum price
min_price.help: Without planner: do not deliver below this price.
min_price.more: E.g. € 0.25: below this price (all-in, per kWh) the battery does not deliver. Empty = no minimum.

live_off_after_restart.label: Live control off after a restart (test phase)
live_off_after_restart.help: Off (default): after a restart live control comes back on its own as soon as the P1 reports and the sets are online (if it was on). On: it stays off and you switch it on yourself.
live_off_after_restart.more: Default off: after a restart live control comes back by itself. On only while testing, if you want to check after every restart before ZEPHYR controls the battery again.

vacation_when_away.label: Vacation when nobody is home
vacation_when_away.help: On by itself after 24 hours with nobody home.
vacation_when_away.more: After 24 hours with nobody home (zone.home = 0) vacation turns on by itself: the planner then counts on low consumption. Off as soon as someone is back. Only works if phones with the HA app share their location.

workday_entity.label: Workday sensor
workday_entity.more: Install the Workday integration (your country) and choose its sensor. Public holidays then count as weekend days in the consumption profile. Without a sensor Monday to Friday are workdays.

curtail_negative.label: Surplus solar at a negative price
curtail_negative.help: What happens to surplus solar when the export price is below zero. Off: it is exported and costs money, the planner makes room in the battery first. Another system: an inverter limiter curtails it by itself. ZEPHYR: ZEPHYR blocks export of the sets' own panels and curtails the inverter: with the switch or with the power limit below (one of the two).
curtail_negative.more: With net metering (until 2027) the export price is rarely negative. Without it, it happens on sunny afternoons in spring and summer. Choose ZEPHYR if your inverter can be limited via HA (e.g. SolarEdge via Modbus), Other system if something else already does it.

curtail_switch.label: Inverter curtail switch
curtail_switch.help: On while the export price is negative. Alternative to the power limit.
curtail_switch.more: A switch that makes your inverter stop exporting, e.g. a template switch that sets your inverter's export limit. ZEPHYR turns it on at a negative export price and off again afterwards. Choose this or the power limit.

solar_power_entities.label: Solar panel power
solar_power_entities.help: Power sensors (W) of inverters, added up.
solar_power_entities.more: Power in W of inverters not connected to a Zendure set, e.g. AC power of SolarEdge; several are added up. Not the PV of the Zendure set itself: ZEPHYR already reads that. Empty: ZEPHYR estimates it from the solar counter (coarser, lags behind).

curtail_number.label: Inverter power limit
curtail_number.help: Number entity that limits the inverter's power in % (e.g. SolarEdge Modbus active power limit). Only with ZEPHYR curtails.
curtail_number.more: E.g. Active power limit of the SolarEdge Modbus integration (a number in %). ZEPHYR sets it every 10 s so the inverter only produces what house and battery take, and back to 100 % afterwards. Needs: the rated power below and the solar power (Sources).

curtail_inverter_w.label: Inverter rated power
curtail_inverter_w.help: Rated AC power of that inverter (W), to turn the wanted production into a %. 0 = not set.
curtail_inverter_w.more: The AC power on the rating plate, e.g. 5000 W for a SolarEdge SE5K, 3680 W for an SE3680H.

calibration_days.label: Calibration after days
calibration_days.help: After this many days without 100 % the planner charges the battery full and lets the set calibrate.
calibration_days.more: Default 21 days; 0 = off. The longer the battery has not been full, the further the packs drift apart. From half of these days the planner looks for a cheap moment or sun to charge to full; on the last day it must. ZEPHYR then does not deliver until the set has finished calibrating (max. 2 hours).

price_forecast_entity.label: Price forecast (jeroen.nl)
price_forecast_entity.help: Optional: the sensor of ha-jeroen-nl, to look past the known prices.
price_forecast_entity.more: Install the HACS integration ha-jeroen-nl with your own jeroen.nl API key and choose its price sensor here. ZEPHYR reads only that sensor and never fetches anything from jeroen.nl itself. Only forecast quarters after the last known Nord Pool price are used; Nord Pool always leads. Source: jeroen.nl.

price_forecast_mode.label: Use in the plan
price_forecast_mode.help: Indicative: the plan stays the same. Take into account: the planner plans with the forecast.
price_forecast_mode.more: Indicative: the diagnostics compare the plan with and without the forecast. Take into account: the planner also looks at the forecast days (by default: the day after the known prices, so after about 13:00 the day after tomorrow). The level of the forecast can be off, the trend is usually clear; with the value Low the planner stays careful. Blocks on forecast quarters stay indicative and do not count in the totals. The stored forecasts give a backtest after about 6 weeks.

price_forecast_days.label: Forecast days
price_forecast_days.help: How many days past the last known price.
price_forecast_days.more: Default 1: before about 13:00 the forecast stands in for tomorrow; after that it adds the day after tomorrow. 0 = only store the forecast for the quality figures.

price_forecast_value.label: Value from the band
price_forecast_value.help: Low is careful: no charging on an optimistic guess.
price_forecast_value.more: jeroen.nl gives an 80 % band (p10–p90). Low uses p10 for buying and selling, so the planner does not charge for, or hold energy for, a peak that may not come. Middle uses the expected value.

settings.vac_help: During a vacation the planner uses the standby use and learns it apart; the normal use profile stays clean. An end date is optional.
settings.house_note: When you usually run your appliances. One tap under Prices and plan lets ZEPHYR pick the cheapest start within this window. Add a new appliance with a smart plug via Devices & services → ZEPHYR → Add appliance. Changing the window reloads ZEPHYR briefly.
settings.appl_after_help: plan the dryer along (once, after the last wash) when you plan the washing
settings.curtail_rated_missing: Fill in the rated power, or ZEPHYR does not limit.

airco.blocked_unknown: Air conditioner · not from the battery

airco.estimate_more: Estimated from the air conditioner's energy counter (steps of {kwh} kWh). Between two steps the estimate drops by itself; ZEPHYR sees a stop at once from the climate entity.

diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.intro: For an issue on GitHub or help on the forum: download the diagnostics. Serial numbers and IP addresses are left out; your entity names are included.
diag.counters_note: Power commands go to working memory; standby and charge limits to flash (as few as possible). Relay counts the switches between delivering, charging and off.
diag.no_events: No events since the last start.

event.second_controller: Something else controls the set too (second controller)
event.excluded_on: Air conditioner outside the battery: {kw} kW
event.excluded_off: Air conditioner no longer outside the battery

diag.shadow_counts: Shadow mode: counted what ZEPHYR would send. Nothing was written to the set; Failed only counts real writes.
diag.profile_source: Learned use per hour that the planner works with. Source: {source}.
diag.profile_airco: air con {kwh} kWh (not from the battery)
diag.profile_learned: not learned yet ({n} of 24 are): the planner uses the mean there, {mean} kWh per hour
diag.profile_hour: {hour}:00 · house {house} kWh · air con {airco} kWh · measured {n}×
diag.profile_empty_workday: No workdays learned yet. Until then the planner uses the mean for every hour ({mean} kWh).
diag.profile_empty_weekend: No weekend days learned yet. Until then the planner uses the mean for every hour on Saturday and Sunday ({mean} kWh).
diag.check_intro: What the plan of the evening before expected, next to what happened. Last {n} whole days; only quarters that had a plan.
diag.check_none: No whole day with a plan from the day before yet. This fills from tomorrow.
diag.energy_sub: ZEPHYR's own counters per set (kWh since the start), with what was filled in after a gap
diag.energy_open: Set unreachable since {since}: filled in once it is back.
diag.energy_open_restart: Restart since {since}: filled in at the first report.
diag.energy_no_gaps: No gaps: the counters ran without a break.
diag.energy_note: Estimated = filled in after a gap (interpolated for short gaps, else from the change in state of charge). Failed reads count since ZEPHYR started.
diag.peaks_line: Short peaks from the grid: today {today} ({n}×), on average {mean} per day
diag.peaks_info: ZEPHYR does not follow sudden rises of more than 800 W (like a boiling-water tap) for the first 10 s. That saves writes and back-and-forth; this energy comes from the grid.
diag.peaks_bars: Short peaks per day, last 14 days
diag.peaks_note: After a restart of HA this series starts again.
diag.appl_empty: No appliances yet. Add them in Devices & services → ZEPHYR → Add appliance.
diag.appl_chart: Power per minute of a run, up to {max} W

savings.title: Savings from the battery
savings.no_data: No data for this period yet.
savings.incomplete: {n} of {total} quarters without data; the amounts are then too low.
savings.solar_part_help: Solar that went into the battery during the day and fed the house in the evening or night, instead of being exported at a lower price.
savings.trade_part_help: Charging from the grid when power is cheap and delivering when it is expensive. After losses; can be negative when the difference was too small.
savings.note_compare: Comparison: the same house and the same solar, once with and once without the battery, with your own tariffs per quarter.
savings.note_fixed: Fixed costs (standing charge, grid operator) are the same with and without the battery and do not count.
savings.note_saldering: Net metering runs until {date}; until then exporting is worth almost as much as importing, and keeping solar earns less.
savings.note_since: The cost log runs since {date}; nothing is known before that.
savings.note_hourly: Days before {date} were worked out afterwards from HA's hourly statistics, with the same method but per hour instead of per quarter: a little less precise.
savings.bf_intro: The cost log measures since {date}. For the days before, ZEPHYR works out the savings from Home Assistant's hourly statistics: your P1 counters (from Settings), the battery's charge and discharge counters, solar and price.
savings.bf_help: Choose the set's counters from the period before ZEPHYR, for example those of the previous integration. Hours without a counter reading do not count; hours without a price get no amount. Working out again replaces the previous run.
savings.bf_done: {n} days worked out ({first} – {last}). {skipped} hours without a counter reading, {unpriced} hours without a price.
savings.bf_nothing: No days to work out in this period.
savings.bf_err_no_counters: First choose the P1 counters for import and export in Settings → Sources.
savings.bf_err_no_battery_counters: Choose the battery's charge and discharge counters.
savings.bf_price_ez: EnergyZero (Dutch market price per hour, fetched)
savings.bf_price_sensor: A sensor with statistics in HA
savings.bf_ez_failed: EnergyZero gave no prices for {n} day(s); try again later.
savings.estimated: {n} of {total} quarters estimated (HA was off, the set was briefly unreachable or the price was missing).
savings.estimated_price: Of these, {n} with a provisional price; it is replaced as soon as the real one is known.
savings.sun_direct_help: solar the house used straight away, instead of buying power.
savings.sun_export_help: Solar that went to the grid; until 2027 worth almost as much as import, plus a 10 % bonus by day.
savings.sun_after_saldering: From 1-1-2027 export only earns the market price + margin + bonus.
savings.note_solar: Solar = what you would have paid more without solar panels: direct use at the buy price and export at the export price.
savings.bf_warn_pv: Note: these counters belong to another Zendure integration and include the panels on the set; in summer that solar then counts as battery.
